articles.title: Take or License: Can a Contract Cap Trade Secret Damages at a Royalty?
articles.content:
由丹尼斯·克鲁奇撰写
这是关于Versata Software LLC诉Ford Motor Co一案的第二篇文章。2026年9月10日，联邦巡回法院发布了对5月22日判决的修订版，仅修改了一句话的实质性内容。法官休斯（Chief Judge Moore和Judge Taranto参与）的裁决未变：尽管Versata十年来一直向福特公司授权其软件，但Versata仍可根据《防止商业秘密被窃取法》和《密歇根州统一商业秘密法》追求不当得利赔偿；8,200万美元的违约赔偿判决被恢复；福特公司对商业秘密责任的挑战被驳回。第一篇文章介绍了不当得利的裁决。

修改的那句话与包含在1,095万美元基础许可费中的履约成本有关。5月的裁决称，福特公司从未“声称”存在这样的成本，这显然有些过分了，因为地方法院正是基于这个理由拒绝了这一数字。新版本则称福特公司从未“证明其无需置疑”这些成本是存在的，这符合第50条的规定。

本文将探讨两个后续问题：(1) 商业秘密赔偿的范围比专利赔偿更广；(2) 作为许可方的福特公司是否可以通过原合同将其责任限定在特许权使用费上（合同中排除了不当得利赔偿）。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

This is the second post on Versata Software, LLC v. Ford Motor Co. On September 10, 2026, the Federal Circuit issued a modified version of its May 22 opinion, changing a single substantive sentence. The holdings of the panel (Judge Hughes, joined by Chief Judge Moore and Judge Taranto) are unchanged: Versata may pursue unjust enrichment damages under the Defend Trade Secrets Act and the Michigan Uniform Trade Secrets Act despite a decade of licensing its software to Ford; the jury's $82 million breach-of-contract award is reinstated; and Ford's challenge to trade secret liability fails. My first post covered the unjust enrichment holding.

The changed sentence concerns the costs of performance built into the $10.95 million base-license figure. The May opinion said that Ford never "claim[ed]" such costs, which was (apparently) an overstatement, since the district court had rejected the figure on exactly that ground. The new version says Ford never "demonstrate[d] that it was beyond dispute" that the costs existed, a Rule 50 framing.

This post takes up two follow-on questions: (1) how much broader trade secret damages are than patent damages, and  (2) whether a licensee like Ford could have capped its exposure at a royalty in the original contract (contractually excluding unjust enrichment damages).

articles.title: It’s Down There Somewhere: Viavi’s Section 285 Fee Award Affirmed
articles.content:
维亚威解决方案公司诉白金光学技术公司案（PTOT），案号2025-1362（联邦巡回法院，2026年9月8日决议，非先例性裁决）

类比是司法推理的关键特征。今天的裁决引用电影《大空头》为例，指出发现程序不能被用作对原告尚未具备的主张进行开放式搜索的工具。联邦巡回法院支持第285条下的"例外案件"认定，将维亚威对PTOT营业记录的拟议搜索比作电影中那群倒霉的闯入者反复将"老大"按入马桶寻找并不存在的钱，引用老大讽刺的回应："钱就在下面某处，让我再看看。"

维亚威在北加州地区法院对PTOT提起诉讼，涉及用于移动电话3D传感的光学滤光器，指控其持有的单一样本滤光器"11246滤光器"，"或与之实质相同的滤光器"。五个月后，PTOT提出摘要判决动议，附有一份声明称11246滤光器并非为被指控设备设计，且自2020年5月以来未被制造或出售。维亚威从未反驳该声明，未曾传唤声明人作证，也未曾寻求针对该声明的发现程序。它也从未从其侵权指控中删除该滤光器，而是保留它作为"腰带和吊带"（即双重保险），同时追求发现程序以寻找其他可指控的PTOT滤光器。维亚威最终以终审形式撤诉，导致摘要判决动议在未曾裁决的情况下失去意义。戴维拉法官认定该案为"例外案件"，并从该声明提交之日起开始计算诉讼费用。联邦巡回法院现已支持这一裁决。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

Viavi Solutions Inc. v. Platinum Optics Technology Inc. (PTOT), No. 2025-1362 (Fed. Cir. Sept. 8, 2026) (nonprecedential)

Analogy is a key feature of judicial reasoning. Today’s decision uses The Big Lebowski to make the point that discovery cannot be used as an open-ended search for a claim that a plaintiff does not yet have. Affirming an exceptional-case finding under § 285, the Federal Circuit compared Viavi’s proposed search through PTOT’s business records to the film’s hapless intruders repeatedly dunking the Dude in a toilet while looking for money that was not there, prompting the Dude’s sarcastic response: “It’s down there somewhere, let me take another look.”

Viavi sued PTOT in the N.D. Cal. over optical filters used for 3D sensing in mobile phones, accusing a single sample filter in its possession, the "11246 Filter," "or a filter that is not materially different than that." Five months in, PTOT moved for summary judgment with a declaration stating that the 11246 Filter had not been designed for the accused devices and had not been manufactured or sold since May 2020. Viavi never contested that declaration, never deposed the declarant, and never sought discovery aimed at testing it. It also never dropped the filter from its infringement contentions, keeping it in place, as its counsel put it, as "belt and suspenders" while pursuing discovery aimed at finding some other PTOT filter to accuse instead.  Viavi ultimately dismissed its case with prejudice, which mooted the summary judgment motion before it was ever decided.  Judge Davila then found the case exceptional and started the fee clock on the day that declaration was filed. The Federal Circuit has now affirmed.
